## Vivani Medical Announces Positive Top-Line Results from SLIM-1™, a First in Human Phase 1 Trial of NPM-139 (semaglutide implant) and Wegovy (weekly semaglutide injections) in Obese and Overweight Subjects


November 12, 2026 8:00am EST[Download as PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_62c8c1a19fc8d0fa14b05d2cbe0d06f7/vivanimedical/news/2026-11-12_Vivani_Medical_Announces_Positive_Top_Line_227.pdf)


*Strong NPM-139 safety and tolerability profile:*


*-0 of 10 NPM-139 subjects experienced adverse events reported as treatment related*
*-5 of 10 Wegovy subjects (control group) experienced adverse events reported as treatment related (gastrointestinal only, consistent with marketed GLP-1 therapies)*


*Encouraging NPM-139 semaglutide release profile:*


*-No NPM-139 rapid drug exposure increases; maximum drug levels from a single administration measured at ~16 days (versus ~2.4 days for the Wegovy control group)*
*-NPM-139 semaglutide delivery was encouraging and consistent with preclinical performance*
*-Comparable weight loss was observed between the NPM-139 and Wegovy groups*


*Clinical advancement supported:*


*-Vivani will advance NPM-139 towards a Phase 2 dose-ranging weight maintenance trial anticipated to begin in 2027*
*-Vivani will explore the potential for clinical development of NPM-139 in GLP-1-naïve patients based on the positive SLIM-1 tolerability profile*


ALAMEDA, Calif., Nov. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Vivani Medical, Inc. (Nasdaq: VANI) (“Vivani” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing miniature, ultra-long-acting drug implants utilizing its proprietary NanoPortal™ technology, today reported positive top-line results from SLIM-1, the Company’s recently completed Phase 1 trial of low-dose NPM-139 (semaglutide implant) and a control group of low-dose Wegovy™ (semaglutide injection). NPM-139 is a subdermal implant being designed for once or twice-yearly administration under development for chronic weight management in obese or overweight patients.


“The positive top-line data from our SLIM-1 Phase 1 trial marks a critical milestone for Vivani, demonstrating encouraging clinical translation from preclinical models to humans, an encouraging delivery profile, and a strong tolerability profile,” said Adam Mendelsohn, CEO of Vivani Medical. “Real-world data show a staggering level of GLP-1 therapy dropoff. By some estimates, more than 50% of GLP-1 users discontinue their therapy within a single year, with gastrointestinal side effects driving much of this attrition. The long-term health outcomes and related pharmacoeconomic value that have been associated with GLP-1 therapy are only realized when patients remain on treatment for durations significantly longer than one year. The absence of rapid drug exposure increases from the NPM-139 group is both desirable and reassuring because rapid increases in drug concentrations have been associated with tolerability issues with other GLP-1 therapies. The strong NPM-139 safety and tolerability profile in SLIM-1 reinforces our belief that NPM-139 may directly address a major reason for attrition in GLP-1 therapies, while simultaneously improving medication adherence and convenience for patients.”


Dr. Mendelsohn continued, “We don’t know of any other company that is developing miniature, ultra-long-acting, GLP-1 implants that make possible a once- or twice-yearly administration frequency, with the reversibility speed of a weekly injection. We expect that quick reversibility will be a compelling feature for certain segments of the GLP-1 market who would like an ultra-long-acting option but would need one that offers quick reversibility, including the approximately 23% of GLP-1 users who are women of child-bearing age due to recommendations against continued GLP-1 use during pregnancy.”


Vivani Chairman of the Board, Gregg Williams, stated, “I’m very excited about the new top-line SLIM-1 data released today and continue to believe these miniature, ultra-long-acting drug implants have the potential to revolutionize the treatment of chronic diseases including obesity and type 2 diabetes. I remain committed to supporting the development of Vivani’s portfolio of innovative drug implants and the ultimate benefits these new therapeutic options may deliver to prescribers and their patients.”


**About SLIM-1™**


SLIM-1 is an open-label, active-controlled clinical trial evaluating a low-dose NPM-139 (semaglutide implant) given to 10 participants, and the starting dose of Wegovy (0.25mg/week semaglutide injection) given to a control group of 10 participants, over a four-week duration. The trial was designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetic profile in overweight or obese participants who are otherwise healthy. Changes in weight were also measured.


SLIM-1 was conducted in a single study center in Australia. Implant insertions and removals were brief and successfully completed without any complications. The Wegovy group experienced weight loss of 0.82 percent and the NPM-139 group experienced weight loss of 0.79 percent. No serious adverse events (AEs) were reported in the study.


Vivani continues to support Novo Nordisk’s evaluation of NPM-139 and the NanoPortal technology under the non-exclusive agreement announced in July 2026.


**About Vivani Medical, Inc.**


Leveraging its proprietary NanoPortal™ platform, Vivani develops miniature, biopharmaceutical implants designed to deliver drug molecules steadily over extended periods of time with the goal of guaranteeing adherence and improving patient tolerance to their medication. Vivani is developing a portfolio of GLP-1 based implants for metabolic diseases including obesity and type 2 diabetes. These NanoPortal implants are designed for once- or twice-yearly administration to provide patients with the opportunity to realize the full potential benefit of their medication by avoiding the numerous challenges associated with the daily or weekly administration of orals and injectables, including tolerability issues and loss of efficacy. Medication non-adherence occurs when patients do not take their medication as prescribed. This affects an alarming number of patients, approximately 50%, including those taking daily pills.
